thread:
maria: quick proposal — switch perf CI to an adaptive kernel-probe sampling mode. run cheap latency/throughput checks first, then only capture full nsys traces when a regression or kv cold-start pattern is detected. keeps artifacts small and focuses on hotspots.

tony: sounds promising. how do you detect the kv cold-start pattern?

maria: two heuristics: 1) if tail latency for p50/p95 increases >5% vs baseline, and 2) if we see a high rate of cache misses in the micro-metrics during warmup (misses/sec > threshold). combine them with seq-length buckets so we don't mix short vs long traces.

janet: do we need separate captures for warm vs steady state?

maria: yep. capture window is: 5s warmup to populate kv-cache then 10s steady-state. we annotate traces with a label: `kv_state=warm` or `kv_state=steady` and `seq_bucket=<32|128|512>`.

alex: artifact sizes? storage plan?

maria: estimate 40–120MB per nsys run (depends on duration and captured kernels). plan: upload to s3://redwood-perf/ci-traces/<commit>/<job>/ with gzip and lifecycle 30d. keep indexes (small) permanently for diff dashboard.

tony: what about kernel selection? we should record the kernel name map so kernel selection regressions are visible (e.g., aten::matmul_fp16 -> cuBLAS vs custom kernel).

maria: yes, capture `kernel_name` and `device` tags in the trace metadata. also compute a kernel-hotspot summary (top 5 kernels by self-time) and store as json next to the trace. sample summary format: `{"kernels":[{"name":"xxx","self_ms":"y"}]}`

perf-ci-bot: scheduled: profiler-orch started for job perf/bench/serve-512 on commit abc123 — pre-checks running

janet: CI permissions — who can read these traces? we should restrict to eng-runtime + perf team.

maria: agree. bucket policy: eng-runtime and perf team only, plus presigned urls for PR links.

alex: gating idea — only attach full nsys capture to PR if the short-run baseline check fails and the regression persists for 3 consecutive runs to avoid flakes.

maria: exactly. the flow: cheap-run -> if diff >5% trigger nsys capture -> run again 2x -> if 2/3 show similar diff, upload and flag PR with link to trace + kernel summary.

tony: can we also record a lightweight perfetto timeline for frontend correlation? smaller and easier to diff.

maria: good call. capture a perfetto trace (text protobuf) alongside nsys, but only for the flagged runs. it helps visualize CPU/GPU interactions.

alex: need a small config snippet we can drop into the job.

maria: pasted below — simple orchestrator config: 

```
# perf-orch job snippet
precheck: run_short_bench --seq_bucket=${BUCKET}
if precheck.diff_percent > 5:
  run_nsys_capture --duration=15 --labels=kv_state,seq_bucket,kernel_map
  run_perfetto_capture --duration=15
  summarize_kernels > kernel_summary.json
  upload artifacts -> s3://redwood-perf/ci-traces/${COMMIT}/${JOB}/
```

tony: looks good. can we compute diff-percent using median of 5 runs? more robust.

maria: yeah change precheck to median of 3 short runs.

janet: also add model version and compiler/quant flags to metadata, otherwise hard to reproduce.

maria: will add `model_id`, `model_sha`, `quant_profile` fields in metadata.

perf-ci-bot: note: storage op will compress traces and emit a small index file.

maria: next steps: i'll draft the perf-orch PR with the job change and a small flake policy (2/3 gating). can someone own the S3 policy?

janet: i'll take S3 policy + bucket lifecycle.

tony: i'll pick up kernel-summary generator and the dashboard diff uploader.

alex: i'll wire perfetto integration and add perf team access checks.

maria: awesome — aiming to land the PR by EOD Friday, then roll to nightly perf pipeline next week. ping if you want pairing on the PR. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy-checklist: new perf job will need role `perf-s3-uploader` and 5GB quota approved.
